pinnedCatalogue: COL26.8 dataset 316115 Amphibia accepted species snapshot 2026-10-02
catalogueMappingStatus: No exact accepted species-name match in fixed list; no fabricated identifiers or transfer to bompu

readEvidence.adultSample: Five measured males, SVL 54.6–57.1 mm, mean 55.8 and SD 1.0; diagnosis separately gives 54.0–58.0 mm. No measured female range in read paragraphs.
readEvidence.identity: 16S sister to bompu, 3.6–4.2% divergence; 4.9–5.2% to somani. Medog former bompu/cf. bompu assignment is attributed to mechuka using available 16S.
readEvidence.larva: Reference SDBDU 2023.6550 Gosner 37, total length 64.6 mm, tail 42.8 mm; broader stage 35–37 comparison 61.4–64.6 mm. Left spiracle, right vent tube, oral keratodont formula 5(2–5)/5(1–4).
readEvidence.distribution: Mechuka source summary about 1900 m, holotype locality 1950 m; Medog 1600 m. Type area grassland beside temperate evergreen forest; males streamside around 19:30–23:30 in late-April surveys, with sporadic calling attributed by authors to unexpected late rain. September larvae in adjacent stagnant pools.
readEvidence.calls: Mechuka account cites older Medog calls under bompu; no new invented quantitative call series or independent frog count.

limits: Diagnostic adult range and measured five-male range retain different scopes
Medog identity is mitochondrial attribution, not broad genomic certification
One staged larva is not growth or metamorphosis-rate evidence
Local encounter schedule is not universal or controlled rainfall response

readEvidence.type: Holotype ZSI A16333 / SDB 2023.6408, adult male, Tiwarigaon 1393 m, collected 24 April 2023; additional male vouchers in 2023 and 2025.
readEvidence.appearance: Live grey-brown dorsum with lighter markings and silver-grey-white iris; white-spotted dark venter and barred limbs. Preservative and live descriptions remain separate; full diagnostic morphology not yet read.
readEvidence.recordingContext: Tiwarigaon 25 April 2023, 20:00–21:00, dry/wet bulb 15.5/14.5 C; rocks and leaf litter by stream. Groups generally 2–9 calls; type 2 first when both types occur. Group duration mean 2776.1 ms, reported range 224.9–5133.6 ms.
readEvidence.type1: 34 calls, mean duration 214.6 ms; 22–35 pulses; rate 122.3 ± 18.8 pulses/s; mean dominant frequency 1.33 ± 0.05 kHz, range 1.12–1.38 kHz.
readEvidence.type2: Seven calls, reported duration 645.1 ms; 32–64 pulses; rate 70.7 pulses/s; mean dominant frequency 1.35 ± 0.02 kHz, range 1.34–1.38 kHz.
readEvidence.distribution: Known only Tiwarigaon around 1400 m near Mehao Wildlife Sanctuary; males under forest-floor litter or streamside crevices, encountered in late April 2023/2025, calling about 17:30–22:30.

limits: Call counts are repeated acoustic units, not independent males
Type-specific and group durations remain distinct
Full species diagnosis, molecular account and skull descriptions remain unread for authoring
Local late-rain explanation is observational rather than experimental
